summary: Iteration 23 · Referral Program (MediCar Plus) — Backend + Frontend tests executed. Pytest: 8 PASSED / 2 FAILED (/app/test_reports/pytest/pytest_iter23.xml). Playwright: TEST 5 (landing capture + auto-fill + trial submit + DB propagation) fully PASSED; TEST 6 (v2.html referral block + copy button) PASSED after overriding hard-coded prod URL in fetch. TWO CRITICAL BACKEND BUGS FOUND blocking the referral reward flow end-to-end (see backend_issues.critical).

critical.issue: Stripe rejects the checkout.Session.create call with 400: 'You may only specify one of these parameters: allow_promotion_codes, discounts.' Root cause: code sets `allow_promotion_codes=(discounts_arg is None)` which passes `allow_promotion_codes=False` even when `discounts` is included. Stripe treats specifying the key at all (any value) as mutually exclusive with `discounts`. Result: whenever a referred customer arrives with a valid `referred_by`, backend returns HTTP 502 'Stripe error' and NO checkout URL is produced — the entire referred-checkout flow is broken. Fix: only add the `allow_promotion_codes` key when there are no discounts, e.g. build kwargs conditionally: `if discounts_arg: kwargs['discounts']=discounts_arg else: kwargs['allow_promotion_codes']=True`.
critical.log_evidence: backend log 2026-07-23 10:02:19,946 — error_code=None error_message='You may only specify one of these parameters: allow_promotion_codes, discounts.' error_param=allow_promotion_codes

critical.issue: When a user upgrades from TRIAL to a paid plan, the existing active TRIAL license is found by `existing = db.licenses.find_one({install_id, status:'active'})` — so the code takes the `if existing:` UPDATE branch. That branch skips BOTH (a) generating a new `referral_code` for the paid license AND (b) applying the referral reward to the referrer. Consequence: TEST 7 second scenario 'test_trial_inheritance_to_paid' fails — the referred_by is correctly inherited on the doc, but the referrer's `referral_rewards` array remains empty. This means anyone who signed up via ?ref= on the trial modal and then upgrades to Std/Prm will never trigger the +2m reward. Fix: run the referral-reward block regardless of `existing` (or revoke the trial first, then insert a new paid doc, which was the original design intent).

minor.issue: The /api/referrals/validate fetch fires on landing load and populates window.__referralInfo asynchronously (~200ms). If the user opens the trial modal FASTER than the fetch resolves, the status shows 'Verificando código...' forever — openTrialModal is not re-notified when the fetch completes. Consider retriggering the status update via a promise/observer or re-fetch inside openTrialModal itself.

`getApiBase()` returns hard-coded `https://project-helper-47.emergent.host` (production) so preview installs hit the wrong host and get 404 for /api/referrals/my-code. Only affects preview testing — once code ships to prod both hosts exist. But it also breaks any pre-prod QA on preview. Recommendation: allow window.API_BASE override or read from a meta tag for stage/preview builds.

rca_of_the_issue: Bug A RCA: Stripe API contract requires MUTUAL EXCLUSION between the `discounts` and `allow_promotion_codes` parameters — passing `allow_promotion_codes=False` still counts as passing the key. Current code always passes the key (`allow_promotion_codes=(discounts_arg is None)` evaluates to True or False, never omitted). When a referred customer arrives (discounts_arg=[coupon]), both keys are present → Stripe 400 → backend 502 → NO checkout URL → referred customer cannot subscribe → reward never fires. Bug B RCA: The trial→paid upgrade lookup `db.licenses.find_one({install_id, status:'active'})` finds the ACTIVE TRIAL doc as `existing`. The update branch (`if existing:`) does an in-place $set → doc becomes plan='STD' but the original referral_code generation (L399-403) and reward application (L407-426) live exclusively in the `else:` (insert) branch. Net effect: trial referrer never gets +2m credit even though the whole workflow (?ref= → modal → trial → upgrade) was designed around this exact scenario.
